title: candidate ramp plan and risk sketch — evan mccarthy
content:
Quick snapshot:
- Candidate: Maya Patel (screening + take-home + 2 interviews). Applied for Senior Runtime Engineer. Referred by Diego.
- Overall vibe: sharp infra instincts, pragmatic tradeoffs, good latency-first mental model. Not yet strong on kernel-level performance micro-optimizations (assembly / CUDA nitty-gritty), but has good system-level design.

Summary verdict (working): lean yes with followups. Hire-for-impact if we pair with a senior kernel engineer for first 3 months.

Notes by dimension:
- Tech depth: + solid distributed systems background (Kafka, RPC design, async batching), + clear on KV cache semantics, + good at reasoning about eventual consistency and cache invalidation. - limited exposure to custom attention kernels and quantization tooling; sounded comfortable learning but no direct shipping experience.
- Latency & ops: + instinct for tail latency and prioritization (p99 tradeoffs), suggested sensible routing fallback policy in whiteboard. + knows profiling basics (perf, flamegraphs). - not specific on GPU memory fragmentation behaviors or allocator tuning.
- Code quality: + clean take-home; incremental tests, good use of mocks. Implementation trimmed scope well.
- Collaboration & ownership: + strong communicator, cites cross-team sync patterns, has run oncall in prior role.
- Product sense & user empathy: + pragmatic: cares about predictable SLAs for customers, suggested a staged rollout plan.

Take-home + interview-specific notes:
- Take-home: implemented a simplified batching proxy; README clear, tests present. Took 6 hours (claimed ~8). Left comments describing future perf work.
- Live system design: proposed a routing layer with capacity-aware scoring + model-variant fallback; called out cost/latency tradeoffs. Good prioritization of metrics.
- Deep dive (code): walked through a goroutine pooling pattern; identified a race we probed (they fixed in follow-up commit).

Red flags / open questions:
- Kernel-level skill gap: no prior work shipping custom CUDA kernels or fused attention modifications. We rely on this expertise across SRE + kernel hires — need to ensure pairing plan exists.
- Prior scale mismatch: most experience at infra teams serving 100–500 qps clusters, not 10k+ sustained GPU qps scenarios. Ask for specifics on scalability work.
- Interview pacing: candidate was occasionally hesitant when pressed on low-level memory layout — might be nervous rather than missing knowledge. Consider a short technical homework focused on memory/perf to clarify.

Suggested ramp / 30-60-90 sketch if hired:
- 0–30 days: onboarding + codebase orientation
  - goals: make a safe small change end-to-end (e.g., add a per-route logging field + unit + e2e test).
  - mentor: pair with Senior Kernel Eng (Diego) for weekly 1:1; buddy: Priya for infra walkthroughs.
  - deliverable: open PR that touches serving runtime plumbing and passes e2e.
- 30–60 days:
  - goals: own an internal performance investigation (p95/p99 regression) and propose mitigation (batching tweak, cache policy change, or config change).
  - deliverable: run benchmarks, submit a proposal doc + change list.
- 60–90 days:
  - goals: lead a small rollout (canary) of a config change and measure impact; pair with kernel lead to scope a follow-on perf improvement requiring deeper GPU work.
  - deliverable: postmortem-style report and plan for next quarter.

Compensation & leveling notes:
- Suggested band: Senior IC (L5) — base range midpoint consistent with recent hires. Candidate expects midband; could negotiate sign-on for kernel pairing ramp if gaps identified.
- Consider small sign-on bonus tied to early delivery milestones (first 90-day impact).

Action items (for me):
- Ask for one targeted homework: short profiling task that isolates memory fragmentation / allocator behavior on a micro-benchmark. Deadline: 72 hours. Rationale: differentiate nervousness from missing hands-on skill.
- Share take-home repo with Diego for kernel-read and quick comments (PR link above).
- Sync with Priya (talent-acq) on comp range + timelines.
- If greenlit, draft onboarding plan and assign mentor pair.

Debrief prompts for interviewers:
- "Which answers convinced you they'd make ownership tradeoffs to prioritize latency?"
- "What would you ask to probe memory allocator / fragmentation experience?"
- "Name one hypothetical bug they'd likely miss on day 1 and how they'd detect it."

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- Follow-on homework should be constrained: repo + dockerfile + script to simulate allocator churn. Keep it ~3–4 hours.
- Be explicit in offer about mentoring pair in first 90 days — reduces risk and increases acceptance probability.

Raw excerpts I liked: "I prefer designs that make the common case cheap — then we optimize the tail when we see it in metrics" — aligns with Redwood's cost-first approach.

Potential conversation points for hiring committee:
- Position as a Senior Eng with a 3-month kernel pairing expectation. Committee should confirm that pairing resources exist.
- Evaluate whether we can accept slower kernel ramp if they deliver strong infra/latency improvements early.

Unresolved:
- Confirm scale claims from resume: which services at prior company handled >1k concurrent GPU sessions? Ask for runbook or graph.
- Does candidate have any small OSS contributions to CUDA/attention libraries? Not in take-home; ask directly.

Final tentative decision (today): proceed to homework, then reconvene. If homework passes, move to offer with 90-day kernel-pairing condition.
